summary: Describes a URN namespace for naming information resources published and produced by the Latvian National Government Integration Project. It was engineered by a consortium of contractors. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This sets up a special name pattern so the Latvian government's documents have permanent names.

questions: how is the ivis urn structured
subtitle: A standard way to name and find resources in the Latvian government.

tldr.problem: The Latvian government needed a way to uniquely identify the many different types of information resources it publishes, such as e-services, schemas and working documents.
tldr.mechanism: A Uniform Resource Name (URN) namespace was created following the standard URN framework. Each resource gets an identifier that starts with the prefix IVIS and includes the subsystem ID and a resource ID assigned by that subsystem.
tldr.outcome: This provides a permanent, unique way to name and locate government resources so they can be reliably referenced and resolved.

today: RFC 4617 is an Informational document that has not been obsoleted. It documents the registration of the IVIS URN namespace for the Latvian government.

sections.title: What the IVIS URN Namespace Does
sections.content:
RFC 4617 describes a Uniform Resource Name (URN) namespace for the IVIS, the Latvian National Government Integration Project. The IVIS creates and publishes many kinds of information resources: e-services offered to citizens, technical specifications, working documents, and XML schemas used to exchange data between government agencies and with the public.

Each of these resources needs a unique, permanent identifier so it can be reliably named and retrieved over time. The RFC defines how to construct URN identifiers that fit within the standard URN framework (defined in RFC 3406) and follow the general URN syntax rules (defined in RFC 2141).
sections.plainLanguage: The Latvian government has lots of documents and services. They needed a system like library card numbers that would let people always find the right one.

sections.title: How IVIS URN Identifiers Are Built
sections.content:
An IVIS URN follows a simple hierarchical structure: urn:IVIS:<subsystem-id>:<resource-id>. The namespace identifier (NID) is always IVIS. The namespace-specific string (NSS) has two parts separated by a colon.

The first part is the subsystem ID, a number that identifies which government agency or division created or owns the resource. The second part is the resource ID, a unique identifier assigned by that subsystem for the resource within itself. Resource IDs can contain uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters like parentheses, plus signs, hyphens, periods, equals signs, at signs, semicolons, dollar signs, underscores, exclamation marks and asterisks. The entire URN is case-insensitive.

Two example URNs are provided: urn:IVIS:000000:DOC-METADATA and urn:IVIS:000000:NDR1021365.
sections.plainLanguage: The name has two numbers: first, which government office has it, then the office's own number for that thing. Like 'Government-Health:12345'.

sections.title: Uniqueness and Resolution
sections.content:
The IVIS guarantees that every URN it assigns is unique and is never reused. The IVIS URN framework says each subsystem can assign unique identifiers within itself, and the IVIS database service can validate that a subsystem ID exists and is legitimate. The subsystem responsible for assigning a resource ID is responsible for validating that ID.

For each resource that has been assigned an IVIS URN, the holder of the subsystem name must operate or delegate resolution servers that can resolve that URN to the actual resource. This means when someone has an IVIS URN, they can use a resolver to find where the resource is stored and how to access it.
sections.plainLanguage: Nobody gets the same number twice, so each thing stays unique forever. If you have an IVIS name, you can ask a server to find it for you.

sections.title: Why a URN Namespace Was Needed
sections.content:
The Latvian government wanted a solution that would guarantee information resource uniqueness, making it possible to find and retrieve a resource anytime. The URN namespace also provides readability and understandability: because the identifier is split into subsystem and resource parts, people can understand which part of government created a resource. Finally, the namespace structure provides a way to resolve resources: one of the URN parts identifies the place where the resource can be found.

Many different parties across government agencies are involved in publishing e-services and documents. By using IVIS URNs, all government authorities can use a single, consistent naming scheme instead of each maintaining separate, incompatible identification systems for their resources.
sections.plainLanguage: Government offices needed a single naming system so everyone could find documents made by anyone. If each office used its own numbers, people would get confused.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: RFC 4617 is Informational. It registers the IVIS URN namespace in the IANA registry but does not define a protocol or Internet standard. The document was submitted by ABC software LTD on behalf of The Secretariat of the Special Assignments Minister for Electronic Government Affairs in Latvia.
sections.plainLanguage: This is an informational document that just explains the system. It's not a protocol that the whole internet has to follow.
